contract.sweep: TestErrorCodeRegistryMatchesSource parses every non-test internal/mora/*.go with go/ast and collects each string literal bound to an identifier named errCode*. That set must equal the `code` set in `codes` exactly, in both directions.
contract.mutation: Add `errCodeFoo = "foo.bar"` to internal/mora/errors.go without a row here, OR delete any row from `codes`. TestErrorCodeRegistryMatchesSource must fail in each case; it names the offending code in the failure message.
contract.class_policy: Every code belongs to exactly one class from `classes`. Connector rows additionally carry CON-07's `error_class`, which is an orthogonal axis, not a fourth state vocabulary. The many-to-one mapping into sourceHealth.state is in docs/architecture/08-cli-and-ux.md.
contract.exit_code_policy: Exit codes 1, 2, and 10 are grandfathered with their exact shipped meanings and are never re-allocated. 3 through 9 are permanently reserved-unused. 11 and above are available to a future phase. No exit code changed in the plan that created this file: 01-06 Task 1 chose option-a, so `doctor --strict` unhealthy still exits 1.
contract.additive_policy: Adding a code or a class is additive and does not bump schema_version. Renaming or removing a code, or changing the exit_code of an existing one, is breaking and requires a schema_version bump plus a release note.

classes.meaning: The caller's invocation was wrong: an unknown flag, an unacceptable value, or a missing argument.
A source could not be read, or was read but produced nothing usable. Carries CON-07's error_class.

A directly observed operating-system permission refusal. Declared with no code yet on purpose: Mora currently INFERS Full Disk Access from an error string rather than observing it, and Phase 3 (DOC-03) owns replacing that inference. Minting a permission code here would publish the same unverified claim in typed form.
A vault or state record is missing or undecodable.
The search index could not be opened or does not match this build's schema.
A failure Mora cannot attribute to the caller, a connector, or the data. A Mora bug.

exit_codes.meaning: Generic failure. Every error class maps here today, including `doctor --strict` on an unhealthy report.
`doctor --pulse`: a source, the index, or a producer is unhealthy. Sick, not broken.
`loop begin`: this period already succeeded. The idempotent skip, distinct from a real failure.

reserved_exit_codes.reason: Low single-digit statuses are widely squatted by shells, test runners, and wrapper scripts. Leaving 3 through 9 permanently unallocated means a future Mora code can never be confused with one of those conventions.

codes.meaning: An unknown or malformed flag was passed to a command.
A flag or positional argument carried a value the command does not accept.
A required positional argument was absent.
A connector process, API, or local database returned a payload Mora could not parse. Retrying the same request reproduces it.
A connector's process, binary, database, or network endpoint could not be reached.
A connector was refused by an authentication or permission failure Mora DIRECTLY OBSERVED — an expired token, a refused credential. Never an inference from an error string.
A source last succeeded longer ago than its freshness budget allows. The data on hand is real but old.
A source was read successfully and returned zero items — distinct from fresh-with-data and from failed. Defined here; emitted on a live per-source receipt in Phase 2 (ISO-02).

A connector failure with no typed cause. Also the read-time backfill value for every sync record persisted before this taxonomy shipped: an empty error_code beside a non-empty last_error reads as unclassified rather than as success.
A requested memory, entity, or record does not exist.
A vault or state file exists but could not be decoded.
The search index database could not be opened. The vault is intact; `mora index rebuild` is the repair.
The index database exists but its tables or columns do not match what this build expects.
A failure Mora could not attribute to the caller, a connector, or the data. A Mora bug; report it.
